_readme: roadmap-supply.py's mapping table for kosher-ai-filter (work ledger #501, filed 2026-10-07).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The project's own backlog (docs/IMPLEMENTATION_BACKLOG.md and
docs/cross-platform-filter-master.md section 7) is the only record of what is left to build, and
until now NOTHING turned it into ledger items. The generators only refiled `Integrate <branch>`
titles, so the loop oscillated between two states: 0 todo items (project-keepalive stays quiet,
measured 2026-10-07) or a duplicate refile (item 500, which had to be kept blocked as a dedupe
guard). This file is the deliberate bridge: one row per unchecked roadmap box, each with a
definition of done that a shift can actually run, so 'file no work' is never the answer while the
docs show unchecked boxes.
FIELDS. key = a lowercase prefix of the checkbox line in src (checked at 60 chars, whitespace
collapsed), so a doc edit that only adds evidence after the em dash does not break the match.
status: filed (file it as a todo item) | blocked (file it blocked on owner_row) | not_filed (do
NOT file; reasons list why). host = where the proving command runs - authority (secratary, which
has a server venv at ~/repos/kosher-filter-ai/server/.venv since 2026-10-07), or zabz-yoga-ts.
dod = the exact commands and the result lines that count as done. Nothing here is filed on the
authority of this file alone: a shift that finds the box already true must say so and close it
with that evidence, and a shift that finds the box needs hardware must leave it unfiled and say
so. Never invent work to keep a loop alive.

items.key: w-back-058 password reset (single-use, expiring) - a parent
items.title: Web: password reset for the parent site (single-use, expiring) - today a parent who forgets the password has no web recovery path
items.why: W-BACK-058, unchecked. The site has own-sign-in (W-BACK-051 done) but no recovery path; the doc names it as the gap a real parent hits. Server-side render + Python suite means it is provable on the authority with no browser.
items.dod: Implement a single-use, expiring reset token on the site (web/server): request endpoint, token TTL, one-time consumption, and a new-password page. DONE requires, quoted: (1) `cd web/server && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` -> all pass, with at least 6 new tests asserting: a token works once and is refused the second time; an expired token is refused; an unknown/forged token is refused without revealing whether the email exists; a successful reset rotates the password and invalidates existing sessions; the token is not stored in plaintext (hash a sha256 of it and compare); a missing/invalid CSRF token is refused. (2) the same suite green at the new commit, quoted with the pass count. (3) `git diff --stat origin/main` naming every changed path. If the suite's file set already covers any assert, say which test file covers it instead of adding a duplicate.

items.key: watchdog service - second service for mutual monitoring
items.title: Windows Phase 4: watchdog service for mutual monitoring (second service parks the first if it dies; each parks the other)
items.why: Roadmap Phase 4 box, unchecked. Pure code + unit tests on zabz-tech-ts, which is the .NET host (SDK 8.0.425 measured 2026-10-07; zabz-yoga-ts has only the runtime and `dotnet test` fails there with 0x80008083); no kernel driver, no signing, no live service install needed for the logic. TamperMonitor (item 366) already restarts the service from inside; this is the mutual pair the roadmap asks for.
items.dod: Add a watchdog service (windows/FilterService + a service host) that monitors KosherFilterService and restarts it when it stops, plus a contract for the pair. DONE requires, quoted: (1) on zabz-tech-ts, in a worktree at the tested branch (its clone is C:\Users\ezabz\code\kosher-filter-ai; the checked-out branch there may be stale, so use a worktree at the branch under test): `dotnet test windows/FilterService.Tests/KosherFilterService.Tests.csproj --nologo` -> `Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: N`, with N at least 8 higher than the branch's pre-change count and 0 failed; the new tests must cover: a stopped peer is restarted, a restart loop is bounded (no infinite restart of a service that dies immediately), a deleted service is reported critical and not retried, the watchdog itself failing to start does not take the filter down, and the pair does not restart each other in a loop when both are healthy. (2) `git diff --stat origin/main` listing the changed paths. (3) `git push` of the branch, with the branch name in the report. Nothing may be installed on a live machine to close this item.

items.key: a stock android build cannot reach a real broker. strings.xm
items.title: Android: a stock build cannot reach a real broker (emulator alias 10.0.2.2 ships in strings.xml, token ships empty, PROFILE_PROVISIONING_COMPLETE declared and never handled)
items.why: Unchecked defect from the audit's own list, and it is the one that makes a shipped APK unusable: the broker URL is an emulator alias and the provisioning completion broadcast has no receiver. Fixable and provable with JVM unit tests (gradle) without a device.
items.dod: Make the broker endpoint and phone token come from provisioning (intent extra / managed config / a persisted provisioning record) with the emulator alias only as a development default, and handle PROFILE_PROVISIONING_COMPLETE. DONE requires, quoted, run on zabz-yoga-ts in the repo's android directory: (1) `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` -> `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, with at least 5 new JVM tests: a provisioning payload sets broker host/port/token and the client uses them; an unprovisioned build still compiles and uses the documented dev default; a malformed or empty provisioning payload is refused rather than written; the provisioning completion action updates state exactly once (no double-apply); the persisted record survives a process restart read. (2) the test XML or gradle summary line quoted with its counts. (3) `git diff --stat origin/main`. (4) `git push` of the branch and the branch name in the report.

items.key: no readiness endpoint (/health?deep=true is auth-gated; veri
items.title: Server: a readiness endpoint an orchestrator can read unauthenticated-safe (`/health?deep=true` is auth-gated, so 'process up' and 'database writable' are indistinguishable)
items.why: Unchecked defect from the audit list. Deployment and monitoring both depend on it, and it is provable end-to-end with TestClient on the authority. Must not leak internals to an unauthenticated caller.
items.dod: Add a readiness endpoint (e.g. GET /readyz) that reports process liveness and database writability, without exposing configuration, paths or credentials, and without requiring the admin scope. DONE requires, quoted: (1) `cd server && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` -> all pass, with at least 6 new tests: ready with a writable database; NOT ready (non-200) with the database unwritable; NOT ready when a required dependency is down; the response body carries no path, secret, version or exception text; the endpoint needs no auth and touches no admin route; a slow dependency is bounded by a timeout rather than hanging. (2) quoted result lines for both the new tests and the full suite. (3) `git diff --stat origin/main`. If /health already answers this for an unauthenticated caller, prove that with a curl/TestClient call and close the box with that evidence instead of adding a second endpoint - say which you did.

items.key: w-back-057 end-to-end web test (playwright, stages 2→7 + one
items.title: Web: end-to-end test of the onboarding stages with one fail-closed assertion (no automated test covers the web surfaces today)
items.why: W-BACK-057, unchecked. The web service is server-rendered (D38-06), so the whole stage walk is exercisable over HTTP on the authority and a browser is not required; the point of the box is that no test covers the surfaces, and that is fixable with the existing test client plus a live server subprocess.
items.dod: Add one end-to-end test that walks the onboarding stages over HTTP against a really-running site process (not only TestClient), covering the reachable stages, plus at least one fail-closed assertion: with the broker unreachable the flow reports unavailable and never grants access. DONE requires, quoted: (1) the command that starts the site and runs the test, and the test's own output line with counts. (2) `cd web/server && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` green at the new commit. (3) explicitly state which stages were covered and which were NOT reachable without a broker, so the coverage claim matches what ran. (4) `git diff --stat origin/main`.

items.key: w-back-059 email verification + configure the one existing e
items.title: Web: email verification, configuring the one existing email path (app/partner.py:631) instead of adding a second one
items.why: W-BACK-059, unchecked. Directly adjacent to the reset item and uses the email path that already exists. Provable server-side with the mail transport stubbed; sending a real email is out of scope and must not be attempted.
items.dod: Implement email verification for the site account using the existing email path (do not add a parallel sender), with a single-use expiring verification token. DONE requires, quoted: (1) `cd web/server && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` -> all pass with at least 6 new tests: an unverified account is limited in the documented way and a verified one is not; a valid token verifies once and is refused the second time; an expired or forged token is refused; the mail path is the existing one (assert the call reaches it, with the transport stubbed - no real send in a test); a failed send does not mark the address verified. (2) the full-suite line. (3) `git diff --stat origin/main`. Nothing outbound may be sent to any real address while proving this.

items.key: boot-start wfp callout driver - kernel-level fail-closed
items.title: Windows Phase 4: boot-start WFP callout driver for kernel-level fail-closed (buildable + unit-testable; real load is a hardware/lab job and must be reported as not done)
items.why: Roadmap Phase 4 box. A full driver load needs a test-signed kernel and a throwaway machine, so the honest scope is: the driver builds, its decision logic is unit-tested, and the load is explicitly reported as unproven. That is still the roadmap's next Windows hardening step and it is startable today.
items.dod: Add the callout driver project (WFP callout at the layers the design names) so that it BUILD and its policy logic is TESTED, and nothing is claimed about a live load. DONE requires, quoted: (1) the exact build command and its success line (e.g. `msbuild`/`dotnet build` of the driver project) on zabz-yoga-ts. (2) the unit-test command and result for the callout's decision logic (permit/block verdicts, fail-closed on a missing rule set, bounded work per packet) with counts and 0 failures. (3) an explicit, quoted statement of what was NOT verified: 'not loaded on a test machine; no signed driver; no live traffic measured'. Closing this item with any claim of a live kernel load is forbidden - if a shift actually loads it on a throwaway host, that must be a separate item with the host named. (4) `git diff --stat origin/main` and the pushed branch name.

items.key: billing secrets are mismatched: lpt_billing_stripe_webhook_s
items.title: Billing: LPT_BILLING_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET empty while the Stripe key is live-mode, so the webhook 503s - prove the current state and either fix or record the exact blocking input
items.why: Unchecked defect from the audit list. The fix needs one secret that only the owner/deploy can supply, but the MEASUREMENT does not: today's state can be read from the install, and the code path can be tested with a stub signature so the failure mode is characterised rather than assumed.
items.dod: Measure the live state before changing anything. DONE requires, quoted: (1) the command and output showing whether the webhook secret is set in the deployment environment and whether the Stripe key is live-mode, with the source of each reading (which env file / which host) - never print the values of either key. (2) `cd server && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` green with the webhook signature tests included, plus a test proving an unsigned request is refused with 401 and a correctly signed one is accepted with the secret present (stub the signature with the test's own secret - do not touch Stripe). (3) either the one-line fix (point the webhook path at the configured secret name) or, if the secret genuinely must be supplied from outside the repo, a ledger item left blocked naming EXACTLY which value is missing and who holds it - an owner row only if that is genuinely the owner's to give. (4) `git diff --stat origin/main`.

items.key: screenshot accountability is dead, not partial. screenshotse
items.title: Android: screenshot accountability is dead - ScreenshotService.startWithConsent has zero callers and createScreenCaptureIntent() appears nowhere
items.why: Unchecked defect from the audit list: 1,836 lines with no entry point, and the 414 green JVM tests never noticed. Wiring it (or deleting it) is provable with JVM tests; the audit is the evidence that nothing calls it today.
items.dod: Decide with evidence, then prove the decision: either wire the capture path behind the consent gate with a reachable entry point, or record why it must not be wired and remove the dead surface. DONE requires, quoted: (1) on zabz-yoga-ts: `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` -> `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, plus at least 5 JVM tests for whichever decision was taken: consent is required before a capture starts; the entry point is reachable from a documented caller (name it, with the file:line that references it); a denied consent never captures; the service stops cleanly on revoke; the store/UI shows the state instead of hiding an empty card. (2) the gradle result line with counts. (3) `git diff --stat origin/main` and the pushed branch name. (4) DO NOT claim an on-device capture was performed unless one really was on a named device.

items.key: pir server setup alongside broker
items.title: Infrastructure: PIR server alongside the broker (BLOCKED on the recorded Q22 deferral - do not build infra while that decision stands)
items.why: Q22 chose '(b) Defer the PIR server - ship a plain on-device Bloom blocklist first', and the doc says explicitly: do not stand up PIR infra without an owner decision reversing Q22. iOS's NEURLFilterManager cannot be configured without a PIR server (measured in docs/IOS_STATE_AND_UNBLOCK_2026-09-28.md section 2), so this is a real decision that is genuinely the owner's - it is already on the queue.
items.dod: NOT FILEABLE while Q22 stands. If the owner reverses Q22 the item becomes: stand up the PIR server alongside the broker, with a health probe and a client contract, proved by a request/response against a locally run instance. Until then the only honest action is to leave this box unchecked and report the deferral.

items.key: modesty model training budget go-ahead (~$850-1,600) + data
items.title: A-BACK-014: train and integrate the modesty model (EfficientNet-Lite0 INT8) - needs a labelling workflow and a training budget
items.why: The box names a spend of about 850 to 1,600 dollars plus a data-labelling workflow. The INTEGRATION half (a model-provisioning seam that accepts a real model) may be writable, but the training half is not this loop's to start.

items.key: whql signing process
items.title: Windows Phase 4: WHQL signing process (needs an EV certificate, a portal account and money - an owner and vendor process, not a build step)
items.why: Signing needs a purchased EV certificate and a Microsoft hardware-portal account; both are the owner's money and identity. A shift cannot start it and must not pretend to.

items.key: desktop duplication api - frame capture loop, dirty rect tra
items.title: Windows Phase 3: Desktop Duplication API frame-capture loop with dirty-rect tracking - capture needs a real desktop session, so the buildable half is the seam plus its tests
items.why: The capture itself needs a live interactive desktop session, but the design (frame source, dirty-rect tracking, back-pressure, fail-closed when capture is unavailable) is pure logic behind an injected frame source, which is exactly how the tamper monitor was made testable. Filed with the on-desktop measurement explicitly out of scope.
items.dod: Implement the frame-capture seam, the dirty-rect tracking, bounded queue/back-pressure and the fail-closed path, behind an injectable frame source; the real Desktop Duplication call may be present but must be untested-by-unit-test and reported as such. DONE requires, quoted: (1) `dotnet test windows/FilterService.Tests/KosherFilterService.Tests.csproj --nologo` -> `Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: N`, with at least 6 new tests: a synthetic frame sequence produces the expected dirty rects; an unchanged frame is skipped; a queue that would exceed its bound drops in the documented direction (name which) rather than growing without limit; capture unavailable -> fail-closed per the design, not a silent pass; stop() is idempotent; a torn/short frame is rejected without throwing. (2) `git diff --stat origin/main` and the pushed branch name. (3) an explicit line naming what was NOT measured (no live desktop capture).

items.key: overlay / block page ui
items.title: Windows Phase 4: overlay / block page UI (pure UI work, no hardware needed; the deny-first design says the hide is what the user sees)
items.why: Roadmap Phase 4 box with no hardware dependency: a WPF/WinForms overlay window with its own state machine. Provable by unit tests over the view-model plus a screenshot of the rendered window if a headless render is possible; do not claim a GPU-rendered overlay on the owner's live desktop.
items.dod: Implement the block/overlay window and its view model. DONE requires, quoted: (1) a build command and its success line on zabz-yoga-ts. (2) unit tests (count and 0 failures) covering: shown for a denied verdict; not shown for an allowed one; the block reason is rendered from the decision, not hardcoded; the window is dismissed once and does not re-show on the same verdict; a missing reason renders a safe default rather than an exception. (3) `git diff --stat origin/main` and the pushed branch name. (4) state plainly whether the window was rendered on a real desktop or only unit-tested.

items.key: performance benchmarking
items.title: Phase 5: performance benchmarking harness (make the numbers runnable and recorded; the device-side gates stay unproven)
items.why: Phase 5 box. The design doc already lists the gates; what is missing is an instrument that runs them and writes a result. Server-side and Windows-side numbers can be produced on real hosts; ANE/thermal iOS gates cannot be, and must be listed as unmeasured.
items.dod: Add a benchmark harness that measures what can be measured on a real host and records the result. DONE requires, quoted: (1) the exact command, and its output with real numbers for at least: broker decision latency (p50/p95), server DoH classification latency (p50/p95), and the blocklist export (Bloom) size and build time. (2) the harness writes a machine-readable result file and the file's path is quoted. (3) each number carries the host it was measured on. (4) an explicit list of the gates NOT measured (iOS ANE latency, memory footprint in the extension sandbox, thermal, perceived page-load delta) with the reason. (5) `git diff --stat origin/main`. Numbers must be measured, never estimated - a harness that reports a made-up baseline is worse than none.

items.key: deployment documentation
items.title: Docs: make the broker README's claims self-checking (probe the live system in a script the doc names, so drift is caught by a command and not by a reader)
items.why: Phase 5 box plus the audit's own 'docs drift' defect. Cheap, real, and it is the documentation the next deploy will follow, so a wrong line costs a future outage (the same README once told an operator a path that would have destroyed the live database). STALE-ROW CORRECTION 2026-10-07: this row originally read as 'the broker README still calls the broker unreachable and the monitor RED since inception'. Measured this session, that was FALSE by the time the audit was written - the README carries a 'corrected 2026-09-14' section that names both false claims and quotes the probes, and the Android package name was corrected on 2026-09-15 (commit 978843f). The row is re-pointed at the live item #554, which asserts the claims with a script, because a documentation claim has no way to notice it has become false.
items.dod: Bring the deployment docs level with what is actually deployed, verified by reading the live system rather than by rewriting prose. DONE requires, quoted: (1) for each claim corrected, the measurement that proves it (e.g. the live health endpoint's status, the container/host's actual paths, the monitor's real current state) with the command and its output. (2) `git diff --stat origin/main` naming each doc changed. (3) a grep proving the specific false lines no longer exist (e.g. the 'not deployed anywhere reachable' and 'RED since inception' strings), quoted. (4) no new claim may be added without the measurement that supports it.
items.hint: ledger item #554; the historical correction note in deploy/broker/README.md must NOT be edited - it is the record of a past error. The live ledger item for this row is named in the authoring run's own stdout and in the journal handoff for 2026-10-07; the id is deliberately NOT in the title, because the title is the dedup key and embedding an id in it files the row again (measured twice: #555, #556).

items.key: cross-platform testing matrix
items.title: Phase 5: cross-platform testing matrix - turn the documented matrix into a runnable script that reports pass/fail per platform
items.why: Phase 5 box. A matrix that only exists in prose is unverifiable; the runnable version is a script that runs what each host can run (server suite, Android JVM suite, .NET suite, iOS core suite where a toolchain exists) and prints a table with the host named per row. iOS extension/device rows stay UNMEASURED.
items.dod: Add the matrix runner and run it. DONE requires, quoted: (1) the command and its full output, with one row per platform, the host, the suite run, and the count - and each row either PASS (with numbers) or UNMEASURED (with the reason, e.g. no Mac, no device). (2) the runner must exit non-zero if any row that is expected to run reports a failure, proven by quoting a deliberate red run or a unit test of the runner itself, then a green run. (3) `git diff --stat origin/main` and the pushed branch name. An UNMEASURED row is an acceptable result and must never be rendered as a pass.

items.key: w-back-055 public content + compliance pages, gated by the e
items.title: Web: public content and compliance pages, gated by the existing public-claims test (no marketing claim may ship unsupported)
items.why: W-BACK-055, unchecked. The gate already exists - the box says so - which makes this a content-safety item as much as a page item: the compliance pages are where an unsupported claim would legally hurt. Server-side rendered, so it is provable on the authority.

items.key: no seeded super-admin. on a fresh database the only runtime
items.title: Server: no seeded super-admin - a fresh database can only be entered with the shared secret as an HTTP Basic password or a manual row insert
items.why: Unchecked defect from the audit list. It blocks every fresh deployment and every recovery, and it is provable with the server suite. It must not create a default password (that is a security regression), so the item is about a documented, safe bootstrap - an operator command or a first-run flow - not a hardcoded account.
items.dod: Provide a documented, safe bootstrap for the first operator on an empty database. DONE requires, quoted: (1) the exact command an operator runs (a CLI or script in the repo) and its output on a FRESH database, with the resulting operator row shown by a query. (2) `cd server && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` green, with tests proving: the bootstrap works once and refuses the second time (no second super-admin appears); it refuses to run when an operator already exists; a weak or blank password is refused; the created row's secret is stored hashed, not plaintext (assert the stored value is not the input); no default credential is shipped anywhere in the tree (quote the grep that proves it is absent). (3) `git diff --stat origin/main`. (4) if the bootstrap needs a value only the owner holds, stop and file the owner row naming exactly which value - do not invent one.

items.key: mitm trust unverified. policyapplier.kt:906-909 logs that in
items.title: Android: MITM trust is unverified - installCaCert installs a CA that Android 7+ apps need not trust, and the only validation script skips itself when not Device Owner
items.why: Unchecked defect from the audit list. The user-visible consequence is a filter that appears to work while TLS interception silently does not, which is the exact shape of failure this product cannot have. The testability limit is real: the certificate-trust decision needs a device, but the decision logic and the skip-when-not-owner hole can be covered by JVM tests, and the item must say plainly which half stays unproven.
items.dod: Make the CA-trust gap honest and bounded: the app must know, and say, whether apps will trust the installed CA, and the validation path must not silently skip itself. DONE requires, quoted, run on zabz-yoga-ts: (1) `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` -> `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, with at least 6 new JVM tests: the trust state is reported (user-CA vs system-CA vs unknown) and surfaced rather than assumed; a device that cannot have a system CA is reported as such instead of treated as trusted; the validation routine runs (or reports why it cannot) when the app is NOT Device Owner, instead of skipping silently; an install that fails is reported as a failure, not swallowed; a re-install replaces the previous certificate rather than stacking; the reported state is stable across a reload. (2) the gradle result line with counts. (3) `git diff --stat origin/main` and the pushed branch name. (4) an explicit line naming what remains unverified without a real device.

items.key: fail-closed layer 1 - wfp session block-all at install time
items.title: Windows Phase 2: fail-closed Layer 1 - WFP session block-all at install time (the filter must block first, then open, never the reverse)
items.why: Roadmap Phase 2 box, and the fail-closed property is the product's stated core promise (Q11). The install-time ordering is pure logic behind the existing WFP layer and is unit-testable on the .NET host; whether the real WFP session behaves that way on a live machine must be reported as unmeasured unless it really was measured.
items.dod: Implement the install-time block-all session so that at no point is traffic permitted-and-unfiltered. DONE requires, quoted, on zabz-tech-ts in a worktree at the tested branch: (1) `dotnet test windows/FilterService.Tests/KosherFilterService.Tests.csproj --nologo` -> `Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: N`, with at least 7 new tests: block-all is installed BEFORE any allow rule; a failure while installing the permissive rules leaves the block-all in place (fail-closed - quote what the code does on that error path); a failure during block-all install itself is reported and does not leave the machine with neither policy; the session is persistent per the design; rules are applied idempotently (installing twice is not two sessions); a rollback removes the block-all only after the replacement policy is confirmed installed; the ordering is asserted on the recorded call sequence, not inferred from the end state. (2) the diffstat against origin/main and the pushed branch name. (3) an explicit statement of what was NOT verified on a live machine.

items.key: shouldfailclosed configuration
items.title: iOS: shouldFailClosed configuration (with the measured reason the iOS URL filter cannot be configured without a PIR server)
items.why: Roadmap Phase 4 box. items.key: i-back-034: url layer: on-device bloom blocklist (not pir ye
items.title: iOS: fix the on-device Bloom payload format so Apple's prefilter would actually match (the served bytes use BLAKE2b; Apple requires FNV-1a + MurmurHash3x86_32 with double hashing)
items.why: I-BACK-034, and the paying half is already on the record: docs/IOS_STATE_AND_UNBLOCK_2026-09-28.md section 2 measures that server/app/bloom_filter.py builds its filter with blake2b(member+seed) and a 0x4F6F5D3F stride, while NEURLFilterPrefilter requires FNV-1a and MurmurHash3 (32-bit) with double hashing, i.e. hashes[i] = (h1(x) + i*h2(x)) mod bitCount. The failure is SILENT: a prefilter built with the wrong hash loads, answers, and never matches a blocked URL. PrefilterHash.swift already implements Apple's format, so this item is the parity proof and the client-side wiring, not a rewrite.
items.dod: Prove the two formats are separated correctly and that the client decodes the one it can use. DONE requires, quoted: (1) a test that builds the SAME member set with the server's function and with PrefilterHash and shows the bitmaps DIFFER, with both digests printed - the point is that a silent mismatch cannot pass. (2) a test proving PrefilterHash follows Apple's documented rule for a known vector: h1/h2 32-bit, index = (h1 + i*h2) mod bitCount for every i, and a Punycoded member. (3) the client path that consumes the served payload is exercised against a fixture built in Apple's format and reports a match for a blocked host and no match for a clean one. (4) `swift build --target KosherFilterCore` on mac-mini-ts with 0 errors - and if XCTest is available, the test command with its counts; otherwise record the test run as NOT RUN and say why. (5) `git diff --stat origin/main` and the pushed branch name. items.key: core ml sandbox testing - can models run inside nefilterdata
items.title: iOS: Core ML sandbox testing - can models run inside NEFilterDataProvider?
items.why: Roadmap Phase iOS box, unchecked, and it is literally a question about the extension sandbox: whether a Core ML model can load and run inside NEFilterDataProvider's memory ceiling. HARDWARE REQUIREMENT, not a deferral: the answer exists only on a real device under Xcode, and Apple's sandbox limit is not simulable. no host in the capability matrix can run it - mac-mini-ts compiles Apple code but has no XCTest and no attached iPhone (measured 2026-10-07), and Yoga's Windows Swift cannot build the iOS package at all (SwiftShims). Same class as I-BACK-031, already explicitly not_filed.
items.dod: NOT RUNNABLE today. Would be proven by an Xcode-run instrumented build on an attached iPhone -> a logged measurement of the extension's resident memory with a model loaded inside NEFilterDataProvider and a pass/fail against Apple's extension limit, plus the model-load success/failure. No matrix host can produce that number; recorded unfiled with the hardware reason.
